cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: You Can’t Leave Mid-Prophecy
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the impossible prediction has been fulfilled, disproved, or responsibly revised.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. Stay until sunset. Gran predicted this stone would hatch, and I promised we'd witness the result.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sun's down. It's still a stone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. Then help me record that it didn't hatch. We can put the prophecy to rest.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll sign, but Gran never said which day.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then stay while we ring her and agree a deadline. I can't witness every sunset alone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You looked so sure raising your paddle, I raised mine too. Lovely auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was bidding on that wardrobe. You've just outbid me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I always begin with storage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then put your paddle down before you buy the matching bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Let someone else make the beginner's mistake of buying a whole bedroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my shoes beside yours for the interview. Very forward-thinking firm.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine are off because the heel broke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I prefer a preventative approach.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then put yours back on. The interviewer is coming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Shoes off for reception, on for the interview. Very clear progression.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay until sunset. Gran predicted this stone would hatch, and I promised we'd witness the result.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The sun's down. It's still a stone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then help me record that it didn't hatch. We can put the prophecy to rest.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep your coat off. The prophecy says this bell-less tower will ring at noon; I need a witness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's twelve-oh-one. We heard nothing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then sign that before you go. We can officially stop waiting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My watch is five minutes fast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me four more minutes. I'll fill in our names so only the silence needs witnessing.

cards.title: Apologize to Reality
cards.instruction: Get someone to apologize to an object, rule, place, or idea for violating its impossible expectations.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. Before your caretaker interview, apologise to that chair. You sat without its consent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It can't say yes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. Then tell it you're sorry for taking silence as permission.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Sorry, chair. I'll stand for the interview.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then apologise for making it redundant. You're applying to care for furniture, and your first solution is to leave it without a job.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: Approve the Impossible Plan
cards.instruction: Get someone to formally approve a plan whose logic becomes stranger each time it is explained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. As venue manager, will you approve storing Tuesday's rain in this cup? The wedding needs a dry lawn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tuesday hasn't happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. Exactly. We'll catch the rain before it learns how to fall.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have another wedding Wednesday. What if it leaks overnight?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll seal it with Thursday's drought. Sign for two dry weddings; I'll invoice the drought after it happens.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You looked so sure raising your paddle, I raised mine too. Lovely auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was bidding on that wardrobe. You've just outbid me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I always begin with storage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then put your paddle down before you buy the matching bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Let someone else make the beginner's mistake of buying a whole bedroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my shoes beside yours for the interview. Very forward-thinking firm.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine are off because the heel broke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I prefer a preventative approach.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then put yours back on. The interviewer is coming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Shoes off for reception, on for the interview. Very clear progression.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tuesday hasn't happened.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I have another wedding Wednesday. What if it leaks overnight?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll seal it with Thursday's drought. Sign for two dry weddings; I'll invoice the drought after it happens.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Inspector, please approve our invisible landing. The museum opens Monday.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's nothing supporting it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We've budgeted enough confidence to hold twenty visitors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How am I supposed to certify confidence?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Sign under 'load-bearing.' Your professional certainty will support the inspectors too, so we won't need scaffolding for the next inspection.

cards.title: You Handle the Impossible Part
cards.instruction: Make someone accept responsibility for the one part of the plan that cannot reasonably be done.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. For tonight's courtyard film, you fold the moon; I'll switch off the lamps.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do I fold the moon?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. Start with the crescent. It already has a crease.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the lamps. You handle the sky.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll do lamps, chairs and projector if you'll own the moon. Can I tell the audience we're waiting for your blackout?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You looked so sure raising your paddle, I raised mine too. Lovely auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was bidding on that wardrobe. You've just outbid me.

beats.text: Naturally. I always begin with storage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then put your paddle down before you buy the matching bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Let someone else make the beginner's mistake of buying a whole bedroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my shoes beside yours for the interview. Very forward-thinking firm.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine are off because the heel broke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I prefer a preventative approach.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then put yours back on. The interviewer is coming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Shoes off for reception, on for the interview. Very clear progression.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the lamps. You handle the sky.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll do lamps, chairs and projector if you'll own the moon. Can I tell the audience we're waiting for your blackout?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put yesterday's missing hour in this jar before lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Time doesn't fit in jars.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then loosen the lid. Don't make the opening smaller than necessary.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You do it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm labelling. We mustn't confuse it with tomorrow.

cards.title: What Rule Did I Miss?
cards.instruction: Find the hidden rule that makes the strange situation consistent, practical, or at least survivable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. The usual arrangement. What keeps the soup inside that upside-down bowl?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've never seen it either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly how we always do it. Then turn the spoon over. Let's test which thing owns down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The soup followed the spoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the spoon sets the direction. Point it into the sink before we try putting it down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You looked so sure raising your paddle, I raised mine too. Lovely auction.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was bidding on that wardrobe. You've just outbid me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I always begin with storage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then put your paddle down before you buy the matching bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Let someone else make the beginner's mistake of buying a whole bedroom.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put my shoes beside yours for the interview. Very forward-thinking firm.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine are off because the heel broke.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. I prefer a preventative approach.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then put yours back on. The interviewer is coming.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. Shoes off for reception, on for the interview. Very clear progression.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've never seen it either.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then turn the spoon over. Let's test which thing owns down.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the spoon sets the direction. Point it into the sink before we try putting it down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your shadow moved before you. What changed?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was thinking of leaving, but I can't find the exit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Think about that bench without moving. Does it turn?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's gone to the bench. I'm still here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It seems to follow your intentions. Think about the exit again; let's follow slowly and see whether it knows the way.

beats.text: Then the spoon sets the direction. Point it into the sink before we try putting it down.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your shadow moved before you. What changed?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was thinking of leaving, but I can't find the exit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Think about that bench without moving. Does it turn?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's gone to the bench. I'm still here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It seems to follow your intentions. Think about the exit again; let's follow slowly and see whether it knows the way.
